708	| DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS | int | 600–3600 (**1800** = 30 s) | data file | Solo recovery window before the death stub, and the VS-B revive window; the solo player may end it early with `give_up` (user ruling D7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
709	| T_apply, GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS *(user rulings; re-review)* | int tick; int | — ; **3** = the minimum over **all** confirm modes: TAP mode is `3` (the first tap is sampled no earlier than `T_downed + 1`, a release frame follows, the second tap no earlier than `T_downed + 3`, so the two taps are at least 2 ticks apart and `give_up` applies in P2 of tick `T_downed + 3`); HOLD mode is `ceil(H_give_up × TICK_RATE)` = 36 at the lowest base hold (0.6 s) and 48 at the 0.8 s default (derived figures, not floors) | calculated | Tick at which `give_up` applies; the shortest `T_dead − T_downed` a give-up can produce over every mode and every legal base hold, so Save/Load's loss floor (`loss_min = GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS + 1` = 4) is a true lower bound; the earlier 48 held only for the default hold and was not a floor *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: registry value 48 → 3)* |
710	| RUN_LATCH_CLEAR | int | 15–60 (**30**) | data file | Ticks of `octant == NONE` before a toggled run clears |
711	| DEVICE_SWITCH_HYSTERESIS | int | 100–500 (**250**) ms | data file | Minimum wall time between glyph-set switches |
712	| NAME_REVEAL_S | float | 1–3 (**2**) render s | data file | Press-to-reveal crewmate name duration |
713	| T_stagger, T_downed, T_stop | int | — | calculated (`controller.state`) | Entry ticks |
714	| death_tick, stagger_end_tick, latch_clear_tick | int | — | calculated | Expiry ticks |
715	
716	**Output Range:** All sim timers are integer ticks and freeze under `PAUSED` (T does not advance); the two wall-time ones (device switch, name reveal) are Adapter/Presenter-local and never touch the sim. The downed check order is normative: at `death_tick` the cap is read first, so a recovery Suit has already written is honoured on the same tick — and because `suit.vitals` runs before `controller.step` (`after:`), a cap rise computed on `death_tick` itself wins. Suit runs at divisor 6, so a rise it would compute "between" runs is seen up to 5 ticks late; that is the tolerance PC-9 accepts. A `SYSTEM` `stagger` that is `Applied` while the actor is already `STAGGERED` does not restart or extend the timer; `stagger_end_tick` keeps its original value, so a stagger never chains into a stun-lock. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from suit-and-equipment)*
717	**Example (give up)** *(user rulings; re-review: Suit ticks are multiples of 6 and the frame/tick fixture is stated)*: one rendered frame per tick; Suit runs at multiples of 6, so downed at T = 10,002 with the cap staying `NONE`; the player's press edge is observed at T = 10,104 and the bar fills 48 frames later, at T = 10,152 (0.8 s = 48 ticks) → `give_up` applies in P2 of tick 10,152, `death_tick := min(11,802, 10,152) = 10,152`, `controller.step` reads cap `NONE` and `T ≥ death_tick` → `DEAD` on tick 10,152, one `request_restore`; had Suit's run at T = 10,152 (a multiple of 6) written `cap = WALK_ONLY`, the cap-first check would give the class member (`IDLE` with no direction held) and the give-up is spent harmlessly. 
718	**Example:** Downed at T = 10,000 → `death_tick = 11,800`. Suit's run at T = 11,796 (a multiple of 6) computes `cap = WALK_ONLY` → at T = 11,797 the controller reads it → the class member, `IDLE` with no direction held (stagger does not fire on a *rising* edge). If instead the rise would have been computed at T = 11,801, the controller at T = 11,800 reads `NONE` → DEAD. Toggle-run: stop at T = 3000 → latch clears at T = 3030 unless movement resumes before then.
719	
720	**D.15 Input-to-first-pixel latency**
721	
722	The `L_pixel` formula (this GDD's instance of kernel D.4, with the Adapter's sampling point fixed) is defined as:
723	
724	`L_pixel = L_sample + L_tick + L_interp + L_render`
725	
726	Derived: `L_sample ∈ [0, frame_duration)` — age of the device event at the physics-callback sample
727	Derived: `L_tick ≈ 0` wall — sample → `Kernel.step()` is the same call; one tick of *simulated* latency by construction (P1 freeze → P2 apply → P3 integrate)
728	Derived: `L_render ∈ [0, frame_duration]` — P5 notify → the frame that draws it
729	Derived *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `L_interp = tick_duration / step_px` — the Presenter draws `floor(lerp(pos_prev, pos_curr, tick_alpha))`, so a tick's motion is spread over the following render interval and the first whole pixel appears only when `tick_alpha × step_px ≥ 1`, i.e. after `1 / step_px` of a tick (8.3 ms at the 2 px walk step, 5.6 ms at the 3 px run step, up to 16.7 ms at a 1 px step); a sub-pixel position is never drawn (PR-4), so the earlier "first visible sub-step that frame" does not exist
730	
731	**Variables:**
732	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
733	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
734	| frame_duration | float | 16.7 ms at 60 fps; 33.3 at 30 | calculated (engine) | Render period |
735	| L_sample | float | 0–16.7 ms | calculated | Wall age of the newest input event when the Adapter samples immediately before `Kernel.step()` |
736	| L_tick | float | ≈ 0 ms wall (exactly 1 simulated tick) | calculated | Sample-to-commit within one `Kernel.step()` call |
737	| L_render | float | 0–16.7 ms | calculated | Same-frame draw if the physics callback precedes `_process` (ADR to verify); next frame otherwise |
738	| L_interp *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | float | 5.6–16.7 ms | calculated | Delay from the tick's commit to the first whole-pixel step of the lerp-then-floor draw: `tick_duration / step_px` |
739	| L_pixel | float | ≈ 6–42 ms at the 2 px walk step (≈ 6–39 at the 3 px run step, 6–50 at a 1 px step; + display scan-out) | calculated | Press → the body's first moved pixel |
740	| L_ack | float | ≤ frame_duration | calculated | Press → pre-play (sound, hand animation, bar): 0 ticks by construction |
741	
742	**Output Range:** Best case a few ms plus `L_interp` (event arrives just before the sample, tick runs, same frame draws, first pixel after `L_interp`); worst ≈ 33 ms + `L_interp` at 60 fps, i.e. ≈ 42 ms for the 2 px walk step (event just after a sample waits a frame, then draws next frame, then waits for the first whole pixel) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; the sim contribution is exactly one tick and never two, because the sample precedes P0 of the tick it lands in (submit before `step()` → `queued_tick = T − 1`, in tick T's batch). The pre-play acknowledgement is independent of all of this and lands in the same frame as the press. With a full queue add `floor(q_pos / 128) × 16.7 ms` (kernel D.4) — unreachable by a single local issuer sending ≤ 2 intents + taps per frame. Anything slower than 33 ms + `L_interp` at 60 fps is a bug in the sampling point, not a tuning matter.
743	**Example:** Key down at 3 ms into frame k; sample at 4 ms; tick k: P2 applies `set_move_intent`, P3 moves 2 px; P5 at 6 ms; `_process` at 7 ms places the sprite with `tick_alpha` ≈ 0.2, where `floor(lerp)` is still the old pixel (no sub-pixel is ever drawn); the first whole pixel needs `tick_alpha ≥ 0.5` at the 2 px step (`L_interp` ≈ 8.3 ms after the commit) and is drawn on a following frame: `L_pixel ≈ 14–40 ms` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: `L_interp` added)*. Key down at 5 ms, just after the sample → tick k+1 at ≈ 20.7 ms, drawn ≈ 33 ms, plus `L_interp` ≈ 8 ms for the first whole pixel.
744	
745	**D.16 Glowstick throw — binding and arc placeholders (Interaction / Suit & Equipment own the mechanics)**
746	
747	*User decision 2026-10-26: throwable glowsticks are Suit & Equipment's deployable lights — thrown on a short arc, landing as an omnidirectional world light. The controller binds the action and hands over the aim; the quantities are placeholders owned by Interaction.*
748	
749	The `throw_glowstick` formula is defined as:
750	
751	`land = foot + dir(aim_angle) × THROW_RANGE_TILES × TILE_PX`, clipped by Interaction at the first wall footprint along the path
752	
753	Derived (the command the Adapter submits on a `throw` press; coalesce NONE, actor OWNED_BY_ISSUER): `throw_glowstick { aim_angle: aim_q }`
754	Derived: `land_tick = apply_tick + THROW_ARC_TICKS`
755	
756	**Variables:**
757	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
758	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
759	| `throw` | action | KB **Q**, pad **RB** (R3 retired 2026-10-27 — design review; ux-designer owns the binding) | data file (binding table) | A **separate action**, not a hold on `carry_drop` *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; a tap/hold split on `G` would delay the drop's acknowledgement by the hold threshold and reuse the hold grammar that means "confirm a destructive verb")* |
760	| aim_q | int | 0–4095 | calculated (D.7) | The throw goes where the lamp points — no separate throw aim |
761	| foot | vec2 int | — | calculated (`body.state.pos`) | Foot origin |
762	| THROW_RANGE_TILES | float | 1–5 (**3**) | data file (Interaction's) | Landing distance along the aim, placeholder |
763	| THROW_ARC_TICKS | int | 15–60 (**30** = 0.5 s) | data file (Interaction's) | Flight time, placeholder; the light exists only on landing |
764	| land | vec2 int | — | calculated (Interaction) | Landing point, floored, after wall clipping |
765	| land_tick | int | — | calculated (Interaction) | Tick the world light appears |
766	
767	**Output Range:** Placeholders; the controller asserts nothing about them beyond integer ticks. Preconditions (Interaction's `validate`): not carrying (hands full → `BUSY`), not channelling (`BUSY`), not staggered/downed, a glowstick available (`OUT_OF_CHARGES`, immediate class). Pre-play: the throwing-arm animation and the throw sound; the glowstick object and its light appear only on committed state (a light is a Pillar 1 anchor and is never predicted — the same rule as the beam toggle, PC-5). The throw does not change locomotion state and never locks movement.
768	**Example:** Facing and aiming E, `THROW_RANGE_TILES = 3`: `land = foot + (144, 0)`; a wall footprint at +100 px clips it to the last free pixel before the wall; the light lands 30 ticks after apply.

770	## Edge Cases
771	
772	Every outcome below is the exact behaviour of the Adapter (presentation side), the Controller Sim or Body's `LocomotionStep`; "diagnostics" names the counter or record the Debug Overlay exposes (`PC_*`, following the kernel's `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` style; Adapter-side counters are presentation diagnostics, sim-side ones live in `controller.step`'s diagnostics channel, never in a block). The `PC_*` names below are frozen by this GDD under the Debug Overlay's channel convention (registry `diag_panel_contract`: the owner's prefix, units in the declaration, not the name); `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` is Ship Body's counter (registry), active in release. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from debug-overlay-true-values, ship-body-and-interior-physics)* Items marked *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26)* fill a gap in Section C and are recommendations the orchestrator adopts unless they reopen a user decision; the owner named "to confirm" ratifies the mechanism.
773	
774	**Movement input**
775	
776	- **If `move_left` and `move_right` (A + D) are held together**: the keyboard vector composes to `s.x = 0` (D.6); with no vertical key the octant is NONE and the body stands; with W also held the octant is N — opposite keys cancel, they do not alternate. The run flag is still carried in the intent. No diagnostics. *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; "last-pressed wins" is deterministic too but needs press-order state; cancellation is the simpler invariant and an option can add SOCD later.)*
777	- **If all four move keys are held**: `s = (0, 0)` → `octant = NONE`; the body is IDLE, a channel may begin, the run latch's clear timer runs. Nothing is submitted beyond the one NONE intent on the change. No diagnostics.
778	- **If the stick sits exactly on a sector boundary (e.g. `θ = 22.5°`)**: on entry from the deadzone `o_raw = floor((22.5 + 22.5) / 45) = 1 (NE)` — `floor` assigns a boundary to the upper sector deterministically; once in a sector the hysteresis holds it until `δ > 27.5°`, so a stick resting on the boundary never chatters. Diagnostics: `PC_OCTANT_CHANGES` per second (Adapter) — a rate above 10/s with a stationary stick indicates a deadzone or hysteresis regression.
779	- **If the stick is inside the movement deadzone while `run` is held**: `octant = NONE`, so `v_eff = 0` (D.4) and the state is IDLE; the intent carries `run = true`; `ramp_ticks` does not count. In toggle mode the latch is set by the press and starts its 30-tick clear timer immediately because `octant == NONE`; if the stick leaves the deadzone before tick 30 the run begins with its ramp. No "run in place" animation exists — the idle sheet plays. No diagnostics.
780	- **If run is toggled on and the player then stops**: at `T_stop + RUN_LATCH_CLEAR` (30 ticks = 0.5 s) the Adapter clears the latch and sends `set_move_intent {NONE, run: false}` (a change of `run` is a change). A movement input before tick 30 resumes at RUN with a fresh ramp; after it, at WALK. A latch never survives a channel start or a context change either (PC-3). Diagnostics: `PC_RUN_LATCH_AUTOCLEAR` (Adapter).
781	- **If `run` is pressed while carrying**: the intent carries `run = true`; `controller.step` resolves `v_eff = v_carry` (carry beats run, D.4); state stays CARRY_WALK; the pressed key changes nothing on screen — the carry-walk cycle *is* the reason, and the HUD does not banner it — but the Adapter plays the one local `cue_input_ignored` click (PC-2; Adapter-local knowledge, reveals no sim result) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: silent ignores are an accessibility gap)*. **While at Suit's CRITICAL (cap `WALK_ONLY`)**: `v_eff = v_walk`, state WALK, `run` a no-op without resetting `sub` (PC-18 test 12); the breath/warmth readings and the visor fog are the readable reason. **While channelling**: `run` alone does not change `octant`, so the channel continues; the intent's `run = true` is recorded; the moment an octant arrives the channel aborts and the run begins. In toggle mode a press during a channel sets no latch (channel start clears it, and a press during one is ignored for latching) *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; otherwise releasing the channel would launch an unasked-for run)*. Diagnostics: `PC_RUN_SUPPRESSED{carry|cap|channel}` (sim).
782	- **If the body moves diagonally into a wall corner with x blocked and y free**: the x-sweep stops at the footprint edge (`moved_x = 0`), the y-sweep proceeds at the diagonal per-axis rate (181/256 × `v_eff`), so the body slides along the wall at 0.707 of its speed; `odometer` advances by `|moved_y| × 181` (Body's BDY-19) and the walk cycle plays at **0.50** pace while the feet slide at 0.707 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: corrected from 0.707; see D.11 and Open Question 22)*; noise is pushed by `controller.noise` (it moved). `sub.x` keeps accumulating and truncating — it never grows beyond 255 because `step_x` is requested and refused each tick; no energy is stored. **Both axes blocked** (a concave corner, or a 1-px gap narrower than the 16-px foot box): `moved = (0, 0)`, `odometer` unchanged, the cycle freezes on its frame, **no noise** this tick (`controller.noise` reads `moved == (0, 0)`, D.13) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics)*, the state remains WALK/RUN (the player is asking to move; the world is refusing); the run ramp still counts. Diagnostics: `PC_BLOCKED_TICKS` (sim, per actor) — a high steady count with a non-NONE intent flags a layout snag.
783	- **If the body walks into a door whose leaf is closing**: at MVP a leaf's footprint is binary — projected as solid on the tick its state becomes `CLOSED` (PC-18 test 7) and absent while `OPEN`/`CLOSING` — so the body passes until that tick and stops at the leaf's edge from it onward; the closing animation is presentation. If Layout later projects intermediate footprints for a closing leaf, the same sweep handles them with no controller change. Diagnostics: none (ordinary collision).
784	- **If a door is commanded to close while a foot box overlaps its leaf footprint**: **`PLAYER` origin** — Interaction's `validate` must fail with the reject token `OBSTRUCTED` (immediate class: ack withdrawn within a frame, the dull "no" cue); the leaf stays open. **`SYSTEM` origin** (a failure cascade slamming a pressure door) — the door's owner enters a `CLOSING_BLOCKED` state and retries the close on each of its hook runs, completing it on the first run where no foot box overlaps; **the body is never displaced** (an uncaused motion the player did not make — C-R extended to the body) and a footprint rectangle may never be enabled while it overlaps an actor's foot box. Body's sweep (BDY-34) asserts in debug when it meets such an overlap; in debug and release alike Body's sweep admits only sub-steps that do not deepen the overlap with each exempt rectangle (registry `overlap_exemption`; the body is still never displaced, and `pos` is unchanged on every tick the actor does not step), and increments the counter. *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; Layout and Interaction to confirm the reason code and state name.)* Diagnostics: `PC_DOOR_CLOSE_BLOCKED` (sim), `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` (Ship Body's counter, registry `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP`: in the `body.integrate` diagnostics channel, active in release as well as debug — should read 0 in every clean build). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from interaction-system, ship-body-and-interior-physics, ship-section-and-layout-data-model)*
785	- **If the actor stands on a section seam when the section detaches**: Body assigns the actor to the body whose section contains the **foot origin** (horizontally centred; the box's top row) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics)* on the detach tick — a foot box straddling the seam is not split; the actor transfers wholly with that side *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; Body to confirm)*. The transfer is a body change: Body sets `pos_prev := pos_curr` in the new frame and `sub = (0, 0)` (no interpolation across frames), `controller.step` clears `channel_ref`, `channel_face` and `channel_body` on that tick through step 1's body edge (the actor's body id changed; a body transfer interrupts a channel; States table) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6; INTERNAL fix)*, keeps `octant`, `carry_ref` and `facing`; the camera treats a weld/detach `BODY_TRANSFER` carrying `frame_delta_px` as a REBASE, not a cut (a pod or transit body transfer is an unconditional cut; registry `camera_cut_predicates`) because the follow target's frame changed *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera)*. The HUD's prompt, if the focused object went with the other section, disappears the same frame (it is no longer in reach). Diagnostics: `PC_BODY_TRANSFER{detach|pod}` (sim), with the seam and the side taken.
786	
787	**Kernel state and resync**
788	
789	- **If an intent result arrives `Rejected(STALE)`**: the Adapter reverts `last_acked` for that intent type to "unknown" and on the next sampled frame resends its current quantised value, bypassing the change filter once (PC-2 resync rule, kernel E "a coalesced intent rejected STALE"). Unreachable locally at the kernel's defaults (queue drains in 8 ticks < 30); it is the VS-B guest's path. Diagnostics: `PC_RESYNC{STALE}` (Adapter).
790	- **If the kernel is `PAUSED`**: the Adapter samples devices but submits **no intents and no commands** (anything that slipped through would be `Rejected(PAUSED)` immediately and never queued — kernel E); the Adapter's in-world hold timers (confirm bar, name reveal) are frozen with the pause (`Δt_eff = 0`, D.10: the confirm bar neither fills nor drains while `PAUSED`, so a destructive hold cannot complete during a pause and be rejected `PAUSED`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; the Chart Table's UI-3 destructive-action bar runs on its own UI clock while `PAUSED` (CT-22) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from chart-table-web-map-and-menus)*; the channel's progress is frozen in the owner's block. On `PAUSED → RUNNING` the Adapter resends both intents unconditionally (resync trigger ii) and, for a hold-mode channel, submits `cancel_channel` if `interact` is physically up — the hold survives only if the button is still down. Diagnostics: `PC_RESYNC{RESUME}`, `PC_PAUSED_SUBMIT_ATTEMPT` (Adapter — should read 0; a nonzero value means something submitted while paused).
791	- **If `LOADING → RUNNING` occurs with movement keys physically held**: the restored block has `octant = NONE, run = false` (PC-17); on the first RUNNING frame the Adapter samples and sends the current octant and `run` regardless of `last_acked`, so the body starts moving on the first tick (resync trigger iii — "the sim's intent equals the hands within one tick"); the run latch (toggle) is cleared by the load, so a toggled run does not resume; no channel exists after a restore (`CHANNELLING → IDLE`), so a held `interact` does nothing until released and pressed again — the pre-play token map is emptied at `LOADING`. Diagnostics: `PC_RESYNC{LOAD}` (Adapter).
792	- **If the window loses focus mid-channel**: the Adapter submits `cancel_channel` and `set_move_intent {NONE, run: false}`, marks every held action released, zeroes the confirm bar and clears the run latch; the channel's bar drains at 2× and the "stopped" cue plays. On focus return it resyncs (trigger iv): the channel is **not** resumed automatically even if `interact` is still physically down — a fresh press is required, because the cancel was sent and a silent restart would be a command the player did not issue. **Mid-run**: the NONE intent stops the body one tick later; on focus return the resync resends the current octant and `run`, so if the key is still held the body resumes within one tick (with a fresh ramp). Diagnostics: `PC_FOCUS_LOST{channel|moving|idle}`, `PC_RESYNC{FOCUS}` (Adapter).
793	
794	**Aim**
795	
796	- **If the mouse cursor is within `AIM_MOUSE_DEADZONE_PX` (8 base px) of the fixed aim origin** (`pos_curr + (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y)`, PC-5): raw aim holds its last value; no `set_aim` is sent; the light, the look-ahead and the focus score all use the held value. Leaving the deadzone resumes normally. The origin does not depend on facing, so a mirror flip moves nothing in the measurement (the drawn lamp moves ≤ 4 px, D.12, without turning the beam); a cursor parked on the body holds the aim until it moves. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)* No diagnostics.
797	- **If the cursor is held still while the camera look-ahead settles** (the cursor 20, 60 or 200 px from the avatar): `cursor_aim_world` is measured against `f_q`, which the look-ahead does not move, so `aim_q` is constant within ±1 unit for the whole settle (120 ticks = 2 s = 5 × `LOOKAHEAD_TAU` of 0.40 s), and the beam does not creep after the mouse stops. While the avatar *walks* with a still cursor, `f_q` follows the avatar at the follow lag: at a steady pace the lag is constant, so the aim is constant; when a run starts or stops the lag changes (≤ 32.4 px) and `aim_q` follows the formula (`(f_q − pos_curr) + cursor_off − (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y)`), within ±1 unit of the computed value — the recorded PC-5 trade-off, a turn caused by the geometry of the camera's trailing pose and never by the look-ahead. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review, delegated ruling R4)* Diagnostics: `PC_AIM_DRIFT` (Adapter — ticks where `aim_q` changed by ≥ 2 units with the cursor and the avatar both still; expected 0).
798	- **If the cursor is over a HUD element**: in `gameplay` the cursor is confined to the window and the HUD captures no mouse input (the hand rail is display-only; HR-11 bracket navigation is key/pad); the cursor's aim point is still well-defined through the look-ahead-free mapping (`cursor_aim_world`, PC-5; not C11's `pose_q` mapping, which is for prompts) and aim continues to track it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R4: the stale "through C11" is removed)*. Only a non-`gameplay` context releases the cursor to the UI. No diagnostics.
799	- **If the cursor is in the letterbox**: the aim mapping (`f_q + (cursor_vp − picture_centre) / k_eff`, window px over `k_z`) returns a world point outside the visible field; aim is direction-only, so `θ_raw` is still valid and the beam points toward it; no prompt can be there (nothing is drawn in the letterbox). The confinement rectangle is the window, not the field *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; a cursor that hits an invisible wall at the field edge would read as aim assist, and the letterbox is only 0–80 px at common displays)*. No diagnostics.
800	- **If the right stick is released**: `live` goes false → raw aim holds the last angle; `live_changed` forces one `set_aim {aim_angle: unchanged, live: false}` at the next interval slot (≤ 3 ticks), after which the sim's facing falls to rules 5–6 (movement octant while moving; holds when still); the drawn light holds its angle throughout. Re-deflecting past `AIM_DEADZONE` sends `live: true` the same way, with the new angle. With `aim_release_mode = FOLLOW_ALWAYS` the stick is never live and nothing is sent on release; with `FOLLOW_MOVE_WHEN_RELEASED` the Adapter then slews the held aim towards the movement octant at `AIM_FOLLOW_SLEW` and sends as D.7 allows. No diagnostics.

Every command carries kernel-stamped `issuer_peer` and `seq` (stamped internally per (peer, source); callers never choose `seq`; `submit()` is void) and may carry an opaque caller `correlation` int that the kernel echoes unchanged in the result or rejection event; results arrive as events keyed `(issuer_peer, seq)` with the echoed `correlation`, a reason code and no display strings; the Adapter keys its pre-play tokens by `correlation` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)*. `TICK_RATE = 60`; durations are in ticks. Presentation reads `previous`/`current` from the read view and interpolates with `tick_alpha` (clamped ≤ 1). Immediate local acknowledgement is presentation's job; the sim confirms next tick. 1001	## Game Feel
1002	
1003	The target is **a body that is heavy, immediate and the same in every rhythm**. Barotrauma's tempo, your own legs.
1004	
1005	- **Immediacy.** Input is sampled in the physics callback immediately before the kernel steps, so an intent applies at the next tick and integrates the first pixel in that same tick; the body moves within ≤ 17 ms plus one render frame plus the interpolation delay to the first whole pixel (D.15 `L_interp`, ≤ 8.3 ms at the 2 px walk step). Acknowledgement of a press (hand raise, tool click, footstep cadence) is same-frame; the *effect* (the light, the progress bar) follows the committed state a tick later. The ack never encodes success.
1006	- **Weight without lag.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: "heavy, not sluggish" had no mechanism beyond the stiff cycle; see the protocol below.)* Walk starts and stops instantly by default (an integer-only ramp at 2 px/tick is barely visible; `WALK_START_TICKS`, off, is the lever if testers disagree); run ramps for six ticks at walk speed before leaning into 3 px/tick; stops clear the sub-pixel remainder so the first step after a stop is never a 2-px lurch. No deceleration slide, no tile snap — both would be uncaused motion.
1007	- **Speeds** (provisional until the pacing spike and the MVP playtest): walk 2 px/tick (2.5 tiles/s — a 13-tile frame crossed in ~5 s), run 3 px/tick (3.75 tiles/s, the integer ceiling the camera's inner box allows), carry 1 px/tick. Diagonals are normalised to cardinal magnitude; the 1,1,2 walk cadence and the run cadence of eight 2s then a 3 (D.3; the earlier "2,2,2,3" was wrong) are what a 144 Hz display will show, and the motion-integrity spike judges them.
1008	- **Facing snaps, the beam flows.** The sprite snaps between eight facings from committed aim with a small hysteresis and preserves the frame index mid-cycle, so a mouse player never waits for a turn; the beam light rotates continuously from local raw aim in the same frame. With a chest-mounted lamp the origin barely moves on a mirror; the old hand-swap jump is gone.
1009	- **Rhythm independence.** Nothing in the controller changes between boarding, the Tell and breach — no adrenaline, no speed buff, no reduced noise. Identical input, vitals and load produce identical motion in every state and at every sanity level (acceptance criterion). Running is 1.5× faster and about 2.7× louder per tile: a real trade in a retreat.
1010	- **The body tells the truth.** Stagger is an input lock and animation, never a physics shove; walk-only at CRITICAL vitals is read off the visor fog and the breath reading, never a banner. Rejections are honest and never shake the frame.
1011	- **Comfort.** Run and channels are hold by default with toggle options; the run latch clears on stop, channel start and UI entry; hold-to-confirm 0.8 s on a linear bar with a two-tap option and an adjustable base hold (0.6–1.9 s; slot Delete 2× = 1.6 s; Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D80/D81) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; right-stick aim has a scaled radial deadzone and no magnetism, snap or smoothing; device switching is silent and sub-frame.
1012	
1013	- **Weight playtest protocol** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; owner game-designer, evidence file `production/qa/evidence/controller/feel-protocol-[date].md`, retained)*. **Target (proposed):** after a scripted 3-minute boarding walk, ≥ 80 % of ≥ 8 testers pick "heavy" over "sluggish" on a forced-choice pair of descriptors (neither "floaty" nor "twitchy" on a second pair); **forced-choice rhythm check:** shown pairs of same-input recordings, one from a calm room and one from a breach room, testers must say which one handled differently, and the pass is a choice indistinguishable from chance (a code review finds no rhythm-keyed value, the structural test). **Pre-agreed order of fallbacks if the target is missed, one change per round:** (1) `WALK_START_TICKS` 0 → 2 (the first two ticks of a move at 1 px); (2) `RUN_RAMP_TICKS` 6 → 9; (3) `STOP_DECEL_TICKS` 0 → 2 (a 1-px settle) — **blocked** until Body's interface carries a motion octant (D.5, Open Question 29), so it is skipped in the order until then; (4) the lamp-housing swivel cue (Visual/Audio) made more prominent; (5) only then `v_walk` 2 → 1 (Open Question 3, a combined walk + carry redesign). A breach-only modifier is never a fallback.
1014	
1015	- **Target acquisition protocol** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (owner game-designer, part of the motion-integrity spike; evidence file `production/qa/evidence/controller/aim-acquisition-[date].md`, retained). The cursor is hidden, there is no reticle by default, and the mouse aim is read against the camera's follow pose (PC-5), so it can disagree with the picture by the follow lag (≤ 32.4 px) and, for the hidden-cursor reference, by the picture-centre offset; nothing else measures whether a player can actually put the beam on a target. **Protocol:** ≥ 8 testers; markers at 60, 120 and 200 base px from the avatar in each of the 8 octant directions, each tested standing and running; the tester puts the beam on the marker with the cursor hidden and no `aim_indicator`; the error is the angle between the committed beam and the marker direction 1 s after the cursor stops. **Pass:** the median beam error is ≤ 15° (the 90th percentile is reported with it). **Pre-recorded fallbacks, one change per round, in order:** (1) scale the look-ahead with cursor motion, so a still cursor decays the lean toward the follow pose (the pipeline's change); (2) re-centre the aim origin after the cursor has been still, so the reference drifts to the drawn avatar (an Adapter change); (3) the avatar-anchored mapping `p = floor(pos_curr)` that the review recommended (the pipeline's D.14b, with the owner of that GDD); (4) turn the opt-in `aim_indicator` on by default for mouse players (still player-toggleable). Resolved 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R18 (user delegated all remaining calls): pre-ruled conditional — fallback (4) is taken only if the spike fails and fallbacks (1)–(3) do not close the gap; until then user ruling D9 (off by default) stands (Open Question 29) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R18)*.
1016	
1017	*Anti-targets*: analog speed from stick deflection, crouch, jump, dodge, aim assist, auto-vault or auto-step, a breach-only handling change, a channel that locks the feet, QTEs.

173:*Acknowledgement vs the anchor.* The beam is a human-channel anchor that may never lie. If the local light lit on the press and the sim then rejected (`CHARGE_EMPTY`), the beam would flicker once on the one object that may not. Rule: **the toggle's sound and the hand's switch animation pre-play immediately; the light itself changes only on committed state** (≤ 17 ms later, imperceptible against a 3-screen-px cone edge). The Avatar Presenter never predicts beam state. **Pose and value split (LO-2):** the Presenter publishes the local beam pose — position and rotation only — and 2D Lighting & Occlusion writes the value members (`enabled`, `energy`, `texture`, `color`) from `emitter.state`; the Presenter's pose write precedes Lighting's apply in the render callback. **Toggle rate limit (accessibility, WCAG 2.3.1):** the Adapter submits no `toggle_beam` within `BEAM_TOGGLE_MIN_INTERVAL_TICKS` = 12 ticks of its previous submitted `toggle_beam`; a press inside the window is dropped (no pre-play, no click, nothing submitted), so input can flip the beam at most five times (2.5 flashes) per second, inside the WCAG 2.3.1 limit of three with a margin (the earlier 10 ticks allowed exactly three flashes per second, at the limit with none) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: 10 → 12; the value also stops the Adapter permitting a toggle that Emitter State's own 12-tick switch cooldown would answer `TOO_SOON`)*. The 12-tick floor also covers Suit's six-tick (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`) sampled-drain window (SE-35). A sim-side guard in `toggle_beam.validate` is Emitter State's to add (Open Questions). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from 2d-lighting-and-occlusion, emitter-state-and-light-exposure-query, suit-and-equipment)*
354:Derived (**I2 in integer form — the one form the pipeline loader asserts; this is invariant 2 itself, and the earlier separate invariant 17 that restated it is deleted** — *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review: merged into I2*): `v_run × TICK_RATE × FOLLOW_TAU_ms + 1000 × LOOKAHEAD_PX ≤ INNER_BOX_PM × 360` with `FOLLOW_TAU_ms = round(1000 × FOLLOW_TAU)` and `INNER_BOX_PM = 300` (per mille of the 360-row field) — i.e. `180·τ + L ≤ 108` at the defaults (`32400 + 72000 = 104400 ≤ 108000`). The registry gives `FOLLOW_TAU` (0–0.20 s) and `LOOKAHEAD_PX` (48–75) independent ranges, which form a box whose corner `(0.20, 75)` breaks the constraint (`36 + 75 = 111 > 108`); the pipeline loader must assert the joint form, not the two ranges, and does it in integers so no float rounding can move the verdict. **Division guard:** at `FOLLOW_TAU = 0` (a legal value, rigid follow) both the I1 term and the I2 term have a zero denominator and are treated as **unbounded** (skipped from the `min`); `v_ceil` is then bounded by the remaining terms and by `V_LADDER_MAX` = 4, and the joint constraint reduces to `1000 × LOOKAHEAD_PX ≤ 300 × field_h`. `v_run` stays a knob whose range depends on the pair `(τ, L)`: `v_run ≤ v_ceil(τ, L)`.

**IA-17 Repair is real, incremental `repair_step`.** For `begin_patch` the hook, at every credited block (IA-14 row 8), calls `check_repair_step` and then M7 `repair_step(subject_kind, id, delta_bp, kind)` with `delta_bp` = `repair_step_delta` (D.1). `hp_at_begin` is read in the hook at the first step, never in `validate` (IA-11a). **Healthy-subject guard (Interaction's own, independent of the Graph's answer to the hp-clamp question):** the hook never calls M7 PATCH when `hp_at_begin ≥ LEAK_HP` **and** `cap_at_begin > PATCH_CAP_BP` (the subject has never been patched and nothing is leaking), and never calls M7 at all when `repair_step_delta ≤ 0`; such a job runs its full duration with zero mutator calls and resolves `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING, delegated G2 (the creative-director's Option B): the former threshold, `hp_at_begin` at or above the patch cap itself, left the silent band open: at true hp 4000 to 5999 a PATCH gained at most 1999 bp, permanently lowered `hp_cap` by 4000 bp and emitted the Graph's patch weep, which a healthy pipe does not, so a one-block tap-and-cancel probed a pipe's true state at the price of a block, the P4 failure Design Test 2 names. The guard is now keyed on the real harm: **both** `hp_at_begin` and `cap_at_begin` are read in the hook at the first step (the Graph's `node()` / `edge()` carry `hp_cap`, as M6's `SalvageRecord` does). A PATCH on a subject that is not leaking and has never been patched is "not a job a patch can do": silent damage is FULL work (Pillar 5), and the job runs the full bar and resolves `NOTHING_TO_REPAIR` identically at hp 10000, 5999, 5000 and 4000 with `hp_cap` 10000, with identical Graph state, descriptors and noise. findings.section: PC-1(b), PC-4 rule 2, D.8, PC-17; interaction-system.md IA-36 (L303); modular-ship-assembly.md L155/L491/L1641; OQ 30(b)
findings.finding: The Controller publishes set_channel_ref(actor, owner_system, channel_id, face_octant), and the facing lock (PC-4 rule 2, D.8, registry facing_from_aim) depends on face_octant being passed. Interaction IA-36 still says 'proposed names set_channel_ref(actor, owner_system, channel_id)' and 'the Controller GDD publishes no mutator for channel_ref'. Assembly calls the 3-argument form. Neither sibling contains face_octant or channel_face. OQ 30(b) says the change is 'done 2026-10-28' and is wrong for this half. A consumer built from its own GDD cannot set channel_face, so the facing lock during weld, cut and patch cannot be implemented from the siblings' text. A second gap: for an ACTOR_SELF channel there is no target anchor, so octant_of(anchor - foot) is undefined, and D.8 rule 2 has no behaviour for channel_face = none.
findings.fix: G6/G1: the Controller is the publisher, so Interaction and Assembly conform. In Interaction IA-36 and the begin_* apply of IA-14, and in Assembly's begin_weld and begin_seam_cut apply, pass face_octant = octant_of(target anchor - foot) and drop the 'proposed names' wording. Define face_octant = none for ACTOR_SELF, and add to D.8 rule 2 that channel_face = none holds facing_prev. Register the four Class B mutators. Correct OQ 30(b).

findings.section: PC-6 focus model, Edge Cases (no focus -> no submit), AC-PCI-115; interaction-system.md IA-2/IA-17; HUD
findings.finding: No GDD says how a self-patch is started. PC-6 focuses only world objects that are in reach, in the arc and lit, and says the Adapter submits only for a focus. An interact press with no focus submits nothing and plays cue_input_ignored (PC-2, L815). The ACTOR_SELF exemption removes the lit check but there is still no input path: ACTOR_SELF is not a positioned candidate and has no prompt rule. Interaction AC-IA-33b and AC-PCI-115 just 'submit begin_patch on ACTOR_SELF'. The only MVP suit repair therefore has no way to be started from the controller, and the lamp-off case in AC-PCI-115 cannot be reached.
findings.fix: The Controller owns the focus model and the interact button, so add a self-target rule to PC-6 and D.9. For example: while the equipped tool has a declared ACTOR_SELF row, the suit is below SUIT_PATCH_CAP_BP and no world candidate is in reach, ACTOR_SELF is the focus with a fixed fallback score above the maximum (3.0). HUD draws its prompt at the chest keep-out position and not only when lit. Interaction declares the row and HUD the plate. Add an AC for 'interact with the welder, nothing else in reach, lamp off -> begin_patch ACTOR_SELF submitted'.

findings.section: PC-7 (L179), PC-7(v), Interactions row 5, AC-PCI-022, AC-PCI-114, Tuning LIT_ABORT_GRACE_TICKS (L959), OQ 25 (not landed from the 2026-10-27 batch)
findings.finding: Interaction OQ 47 declined both Controller asks: the reason stays BUSY (a separate MOVING reason is declined; the HUD never reads the reason), and LIT_ABORT_GRACE_TICKS is not adopted at MVP (default 0, opt-in). The Controller still says begin_* is 'rejected at once with reason MOVING', AC-PCI-022 expects Rejected(MOVING), the Tuning row has default 30 and 'proposed', AC-PCI-114 assumes grace 30, and OQ 25(i)(ii) are still open asks. AC-PCI-022 would fail against the real Interaction (G1: the owner's answer stands).
findings.fix: AC-PCI-022 oracle -> Rejected(BUSY) with focus_view.press_blocked_moving as the only non-audio tell. Set the knob default to 0 (accessibility extension, owned by Interaction). Retag AC-PCI-114 as the opt-in extension case. Close OQ 25 as 'declined by Interaction OQ 47, Controller conforms'. Reword PC-7 and the Edge Case.

findings.section: PC-5 'Two consumers' (L167), D.7b (L518/L528 hand-off), Tuning L950, OQ 23, OQ 28(i), OQ 30(a) (not landed)
findings.finding: The text still quotes the look-ahead weight as smoothstep(V_WALK, V_RUN, |v|) and lists the diagonal-walk misfire as an open pipeline ask. The pipeline (L458, L463) and registry camera_lookahead (L3329) now key w on loco_state == RUN with moved-in-last-3-ticks, and the pipeline's D.7 aim row and D.14b are already conformed. OQ 23 'still open on the pipeline side' is also stale. AC-PCI-092's numbers still hold.
findings.fix: Rewrite the quotes to the pipeline's current r = 1 iff loco_state == RUN and the avatar moved in the last 3 ticks. Delete the hand-off paragraph and mark OQ 23, OQ 28(i) and OQ 30(a) done.

findings.section: PC-5 mouse aim, D.7, AC-PCI-056/059 (not landed; the CD's top feel risk)
findings.finding: AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos_curr) + (0, Y) is tick-quantised, but f_q and the sprite are per-frame. At render rates above the tick rate, or while running, r = cursor_aim_world - AIM_ORIGIN steps by up to v_run = 3 px per tick against a smooth f_q. At a 30 px cursor distance that is about 5.7 degrees of sawtooth in the drawn beam, which is the Pillar 1 anchor. Nothing in the document mentions it.
findings.fix: Take the Presenter-local raw aim (the drawn beam and look-ahead) from the interpolated floored position, floor(lerp(pos_prev, pos_curr, alpha)) + (0, Y). Committed set_aim may keep pos_curr. Update the pipeline D.14b description to match. Add an AC with a 144 fps frame schedule: raw aim varies by <= 1 unit between ticks with a still cursor and a running avatar. Otherwise record the sawtooth as a named spike item.

findings.section: PC-17 / D.4 (walk_ticks, ramp_ticks), AC-PCI-193
findings.finding: walk_ticks is 'ticks since octant left NONE, 0-unbounded' and is persisted and hashed in controller.state. A snapshot rests it at 0 and the replay restarts counting at the resync. The uninterrupted control keeps counting from before T = 500. state_hash(PERSIST, 1100) therefore differs (about 600 against 1100 minus walk start), so AC-PCI-193 cannot pass as written. Only ramp_ticks was avoided, by the walking-never-running fixture.
findings.fix: Saturate walk_ticks at WALK_START_TICKS and ramp_ticks at RUN_RAMP_TICKS (state this in D.4 and PC-17, and change 'unbounded' to the saturated range). Both counters then converge to the control. Add a boundary AC.

findings.section: D.14 second example (L718), Edge Cases (previous log item)
findings.finding: The first example was fixed, but the second still has downed at T = 10,000 (not a multiple of 6), Suit writing at 11,796 with the controller 'reading it at 11,797', and 11,801 (not a Suit tick). With controller.step 'after: suit.vitals' the controller reads the cap on the same tick, 11,796. This contradicts D.14's own Output Range ('a cap rise computed on death_tick itself wins').
findings.fix: Rewrite with downed at T = 10,002, death_tick 11,802, Suit write at 11,796 read at 11,796, and the DEAD case at a rise computed at 11,808.

findings.section: AC-PCI-175, Acceptance Criteria stale text
findings.finding: AC-PCI-175 says 'C11 yields a world point outside the field', but mouse aim has used cursor_aim_world (f_q + cursor_off, pipeline D.14b) since R4, and C11/pose_q is for prompts only. The AC would pass the wrong mapping.
findings.fix: Replace 'C11 yields' with 'cursor_aim_world = f_q + (cursor_vp - picture_centre)/k_eff yields'.

findings.section: OQ 24 / Edge Cases L824 / AC-PCI-116 (dark port; not landed)
findings.finding: The dark-port dead end is still 'open on Interaction and Suit'. Boarding closed only the dock console (pod glow) and assumes top_up at 'a lit BATTERY port at home'. No sibling guarantees a lit fixture at ports (checked Derelict Authoring, Assembly, Emitter State). With an empty cell, no glowstick and a dark port, an autosave restore can return the player to the same state (a restore loop). R21 says nothing may stay open.
findings.fix: Record a delegated R21 ruling that preserves prior rulings with the least new content: every home-ship O2_TANK and BATTERY port carries a self-powered status glow (the same mechanism as the X2 dock glow, with a Derelict Authoring and Layout placement lint). Derelict ports may be dark, because that is a priced risk, not a loop. Keep AC-PCI-116 as the derelict case.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria: AC-PCI-157, Performance budget (R12)
findings.finding: AC-PCI-157 (median <= 42 ms, P90 <= 50 ms) is a wall-clock figure on an unnamed 'dev build'. R12 requires RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK on a release export. At the Deck's 30 fps target the worst case is about 2 x 33.3 ms + L_interp, so 42 ms cannot hold there.
findings.fix: State the machines and build, move the AC under the Performance block, and give a Deck figure derived from D.15: median about 50 ms, P90 about 75 ms (pending spike).

findings.section: PC-5 cursor warp (i)-(ii), D.7 [UNV], AC-PCI-059/060/172
findings.finding: R4 requires an in-engine verification AC if the cursor unit cannot be settled. Zero hits for get_mouse_position, warp_mouse and physical_keycode in docs/engine-reference/godot/. The cursor-unit AC lives in the pipeline, which is acceptable. The warp_mouse coordinate space used by warps (i) and (ii) has no AC in either GDD: AC-059/060 run against a solver stub and AC-172 against a fixture.
findings.fix: Add a manual in-engine AC: warp to a known window px, read back Input mouse position under canvas_items at k = 2, 3 and 4, and assert the round trip is within 1 px. Mark the claim [UNV] until it passes.

findings.section: Untestable ACs, with rewrites
findings.finding: AC-PCI-182 'the bracket shows then hides' has no measurable criterion. AC-PCI-165 ends 'the spike reports whether ... reads as a visible staircase', which is not pass/fail. AC-PCI-055 'three distinct footstep cues are audible' has no threshold (it correctly defers dB to AA-31).
findings.fix: AC-PCI-182 -> 'GIVEN a 60 fps capture, WHEN a key or pad navigation press occurs THEN the HR-11 bracket is drawn on the focused plate within 1 frame, and WHEN the mouse moves >= 1 physical px THEN it is hidden within 1 frame; capture retained'. AC-PCI-165 -> keep only the auto step property (no backward or 2-px step) and move the staircase judgement to the spike item. AC-PCI-055 -> 'the three cue ids are distinct and the run-to-walk loudness delta is >= the AA-31 threshold'.

findings.section: Stale-text sweep (from the 2026-10-27 log, not landed)
findings.finding: L17 'Sixteen systems' (Dependencies lists 22). Interactions rows 4, 5, 7, 9, 13 and 17 are tagged 'provisional' although the siblings are designed. 30 references to 'Section B/C/D/E/G/H' for unlettered headings. PC-6 L177 still says CONFIRM_HOLD_S '(0.6-1.2)' (range is 0.6-1.9). Duplicate consulted-specialists preamble L55/L57. UI Requirements L1021 'three surfaces' lists four. PC_RUN_SUPPRESSED{carry|cap|channel} (L781) lacks heavy, which AC-PCI-147 uses. The States row RUN -> WALK on cap WALK_ONLY (L275) is unreachable because the stagger fires first. AC-PCI-223/224 are numbered after 151. Overview L23 still calls the Body boundary 'open ... provisional'. Header 'Last Verified 2026-10-26' predates three passes.
findings.fix: One sweep. Grep the old wording after each edit (G3).

findings.section: Registry / cross-GDD naming, R9, R2
findings.finding: AIM_ORIGIN_Y (-35) is quoted by the pipeline D.14b but not registered. The four Controller Class B mutators have no registry entity (Interaction's open_channel is registered). confirm_view versus input_view is a registered alias that Interaction IA-41 and HUD have not conformed to. Settings & Input Rebinding, Co-op Session and Accessibility Settings are listed with interfaces but not labelled 'undesigned, provisional contract' (R9). The correlation counter should start at 1 because the kernel treats 0 as 'none' (L87). The D.13 example (run in 160 ticks) is 162 ticks including the 6 ramp ticks.
findings.fix: Register the knobs and mutators. Add the R9 label. State the correlation start value.

input.summary: Verdict: NEEDS REVISION. Section by section, the formulas check out at registry defaults: D.1-D.3, D.9 and D.10 recompute correctly, and registry values match (V_*, NOISE_PER_TICK, CONFIRM_HOLD_S, HOLD_EFF_MAX_S, GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS, BEAM_TOGGLE_MIN_INTERVAL_TICKS). Missing GDDs (Settings, Co-op, Accessibility) are undesigned VS/Alpha and not blockers (R9). No edits made.

Interaction AC-IA-33b and AC-PCI-115 just 'submit begin_patch on ACTOR_SELF'. For example: while the equipped tool has a declared ACTOR_SELF row, the suit is below SUIT_PATCH_CAP_BP and no world candidate is in reach, ACTOR_SELF is the focus with a fixed fallback score above the maximum (3.0). HUD draws its prompt at the chest keep-out position and not only when lit. Interaction declares the row and HUD the plate. Add an AC for 'interact with the welder, nothing else in reach, lamp off -> begin_patch ACTOR_SELF submitted'.

findings.section: PC-5 mouse aim, D.7, AC-PCI-056/059 (not landed; the CD's top feel risk)
findings.finding: AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos_curr) + (0, Y) is tick-quantised, but f_q and the sprite are per-frame. At render rates above the tick rate, or while running, r = cursor_aim_world - AIM_ORIGIN steps by up to v_run = 3 px per tick against a smooth f_q. At a 30 px cursor distance that is about 5.7 degrees of sawtooth in the drawn beam, which is the Pillar 1 anchor. Nothing in the document mentions it.
findings.fix: Take the Presenter-local raw aim (the drawn beam and look-ahead) from the interpolated floored position, floor(lerp(pos_prev, pos_curr, alpha)) + (0, Y). Committed set_aim may keep pos_curr. Update the pipeline D.14b description to match. Add an AC with a 144 fps frame schedule: raw aim varies by <= 1 unit between ticks with a still cursor and a running avatar. Otherwise record the sawtooth as a named spike item.

findings.section: PC-17 / D.4 (walk_ticks, ramp_ticks), AC-PCI-193
findings.finding: walk_ticks is 'ticks since octant left NONE, 0-unbounded' and is persisted and hashed in controller.state. A snapshot rests it at 0 and the replay restarts counting at the resync. The uninterrupted control keeps counting from before T = 500. state_hash(PERSIST, 1100) therefore differs (about 600 against 1100 minus walk start), so AC-PCI-193 cannot pass as written. Only ramp_ticks was avoided, by the walking-never-running fixture.
findings.fix: Saturate walk_ticks at WALK_START_TICKS and ramp_ticks at RUN_RAMP_TICKS (state this in D.4 and PC-17, and change 'unbounded' to the saturated range). Both counters then converge to the control. Add a boundary AC.

findings.fix: Rewrite with downed at T = 10,002, death_tick 11,802, Suit write at 11,796 read at 11,796, and the DEAD case at a rise computed at 11,808.

findings.fix: Replace 'C11 yields' with 'cursor_aim_world = f_q + (cursor_vp - picture_centre)/k_eff yields'.
